title: The Greek alphabet
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: The Greek letters turn up all over: in math (π, Σ, θ), science (α, β and γ rays, μ for micro), college names and the roots of thousands of English words. The alphabet itself is named for its first two letters.

How to hold it: Many letters look like ours (A, B, E, Z, I, K, M, N, O, T), so start by sorting: the look-alikes, the false friends that look like ours but sound different (H is the vowel eta, P is r, X is ch), and the new shapes (Γ, Δ, Θ, Λ, Ξ, Π, Σ, Φ, Ψ, Ω). Then learn the order in chunks of five or so, saying the names in rhythm as a chant. Write each letter by hand as you say it: the motion, the picture and the sound together make a strong memory.
